text.p: French tobacco group Seita said after reporting a rise in first half profits on Wednesday that the outlook for 1996 as a whole was good.
"The outlook for 1996 for Seita looks good," it said in a statement showing a 24 percent rise in net attributable profit.
"Seita continues to pursue its dual strategy of strengthening its market positions in France and expanding outside of France through acquisitions," it said.
"On Sept 23 1996, in accordance with these objectives, Seita put in an offer to acquire a majority stake in Tabaqeuira, the Portuguese national tobacco company," it added. bfl

Seita said a January retail price rise helped to stabilise the market positions of the various tobacco manufacturers and allowed the group to increase margins. "Recent product launches, particularly Gauloises Blondes in 25-packs, have enabled Seita to stabilise its share of the buoyant cigarette market segment," it said.
The group added that sales outside France continued to make satisfactory progress.
"Efforts to contain operating costs will continue," it said.
The group said it made an exceptional gain of 13.3 million francs on a second-round sale of Seita shares to employees.
